Bottom panel: two-state employment-exit probability X_t plotted against three-state EU transition probability (1-e^{-lambda^EU})

structural_features_missing: Dual (twin) y-axes: the claim describes F_t/X_t on the left axis and the UE/EU transition probability on a separate right axis; the produced figure puts both series on a single shared axis per panel, so a level offset is visible rather than an overlay

Full 1967Q2-2010Q4 span: the overlap sample ends at 2004Q4 (n=151), so the described notable divergence in the last two years of the sample (X_t returning to pre-recession level while EU stays elevated, ~2009-2010) is not shown

rationale: output/figure4.pdf was produced and is the correct figure: two stacked panels, the top comparing the two-state job-finding probability F_t with the three-state UE transition probability (1-e^{-lambda^UE}), and the bottom comparing the two-state exit probability X_t with the three-state EU transition probability (1-e^{-lambda^EU}). The core assertion of the claim -- that the two-state and three-state measures move together closely despite being built from different data -- is clearly reproduced and quantified in output/figure4.json (corr_F_UE=0.947, corr_X_EU=0.850); the cyclical peaks/troughs of each pair track visibly through 1970, 1975, 1982, the early-1990s and early-2000s recessions. However, two described structural features are not reproduced. First, the paper's dual-axis layout is not implemented -- both series share one y-axis per panel, so the two curves sit at offset levels rather than overlaid. Second, and more importantly, the overlap sample terminates at 2004Q4 (overlap_sample '1967.25-2004.75', n_quarters=151), because as fix_severity.json notes the microdata shares only cover through 2005M1; consequently the specific feature the verification instruction highlights -- the notable divergence in the last two years where X_t falls back to pre-recession level while EU stays elevated (2009-2010) -- is entirely absent from the produced figure. The figure supports the main co-movement claim but omits described features, so it is a partial match.
